samples.verdict_reason: A caller-supplied endpoint and session are used to POST a traversal filename and recurring root identity-output job outside the server upload boundary. Authorized assessment is plausible but unestablished. Target vulnerability, permissions, cron availability and runtime success are unknown.
samples.remaining_disagreement: Rule findings are hostile. The JavaScript ML classifier is suspicious; the Python and Go classifiers are benign. The installed v18 model reports missing newer v21 feature support.
samples.hostile_coverage_goal: Two distinct supported attack results: traversal-driven remote execution and recurring cron persistence. Serialization and identity-output probes are covered as notable capabilities. No additional hostile action, payload, exfiltration, evasion or cleanup is evidenced; adding a third hostile rule would duplicate an existing result or infer unsupported intent.

execution_trace.javascript: Statically traced Buffer allocation, five loop iterations of writeUInt32BE and Buffer.concat(header, filename, body). No JavaScript runtime available.
execution_trace.python: Executed original source with HTTPConnection replaced by an in-memory capture.
execution_trace.go: Compiled the unchanged body with only main renamed so a harness could install an in-memory RoundTripper.
execution_trace.obfuscation: None. UTF-8 conversion and binary integer framing are ordinary serialization.
execution_trace.execution_effect: Attempts one authenticated upload; target cron, if successfully planted and trusted, runs id through its shell every minute and overwrites a local output file. No local execution API, credential theft, output retrieval, network exfiltration, cleanup or second stage exists in these sources.

identity_comparison.inference: The five big-endian fields, PublicLink operation/step, port 5800, session cookie and traversal-to-cron shape match this published protocol. This is technique identification, not proof of source provenance, affected server version, registry package identity or malicious deployment.

corrections.reason: Bounded co-occurrence proves no filename-to-request data flow. local-path-binary-post.py has an unrelated local parent path and uploads report.txt. Matcher/scope preserved; both exact consumers updated. No directory/ancestor selector referenced the old objective leaf.

Retains ! format support and adds equivalent > formats. Argument zero is now required: struct.pack("<4s", b"!abc") was a false big-endian match. No exact consumers existed; directory membership and notable severity are unchanged.

mail.body = message satisfies the unchanged AST matcher without HTTP. Both exact consumers updated; the raw-IP POST consumer now requires Net::HTTP POST evidence. Generic POST ancestor consumers must not use a generic body property setter as proof of POST. Positive HTTP request coverage was tested outside collector-path suppressors and in the existing Foxtailflow archive.

testing.low_tier_reporting_changes: The engine changes low-tier fallback metadata when a new notable behavior becomes available; this is not lost attack coverage.

post_leaf_audit.action: Moved the proven generic Ruby body-field assignment out of the HTTP POST leaf; no rule deletion, artificial split or budget increase.
